items.item_text: Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training.
Minimum 8 years of experience working within the UC system or other institution of higher education.
Demonstrated experience and commitment to working in collaborative interdisciplinary teams and in positions with shared authority for accomplishing program goals.

The Research Policy Manager is a subject matter expert and leader who provides expertise on a variety of research policy issues, including issues related to sponsors of research (e.g., federal, state, industry and non-profit), intellectual property policy, material transfers, clinical trials, contract and grant functions, and general research administration. The Research Policy Manager frequently problem-solves and analyzes unique issues or problems without guiding precedent/structure. The Research Policy Manager manages activities and works collaboratively with others on issues that cross content areas, may formulate strategies, and administer policies, processes, and resources, and functions with a high degree of autonomy.

40% Systemwide Lead on Research Policy Issues: Provides leadership and support on matters relating to the administration of research agreements and difficult or unique issues pertaining to contracting with research sponsors/collaborators. Provides leadership to and/or participates on project teams and work groups, with members drawn from campuses and OP, to address specific problems or issues, create efficiencies, promote best practices, and facilitate systemwide communication and collaboration. Develops systemwide UC policies and guidance that facilitate high quality research while complying with legal, ethical, and regulatory standards. Provides information, analysis, interpretation, guidance on UC policies and external rules and regulations related to research.

This is a California-based, remote position. Although the role is remote, the selected candidate must reside in California and be willing to cover their own travel expenses when travel to Oakland is required for business meetings.

40% Addresses Issues Related to Research Sponsors: Negotiates systemwide master, template agreements, and complex campus agreements, as needed. Reviews campus requests for exception to UC policy on specific cases and recommend approval or denial.

10% Monitor in respective area(s) the external and internal environment for trends, state, and national issues, and proposed and enacted changes to regulations, legislation, and other requirements that affect UC's research activities. Develops and conducts training on emerging policy issues and compliance with external and internal requirements.
5% Represents UC's interests in meeting with agencies, associations, and government entities to advance policy positions.
5% May function as a lead with less experienced staff members.
Advanced knowledge of academic policies and procedures at UC or in higher education in general, including its priorities, vision, mission, goals, objectives, and infrastructure.
Demonstrated excellent written and oral communication skills.

Demonstrated skills developing, organizing, and disseminating complex and technical information, resources, training, and other materials that is appropriately presented and effectively received by target constituencies.
Advanced skills to read, interpret, understand and respond to pending and proposed legislation, including skills to write effective position statements and draft compliant related policies.

Interpersonal communications skills and political acumen to effectively represent the University, build strong working internal and external relationships at all levels, including with research administrators and managers, University leadership, researchers, and sponsor representatives.

Excellent analytical skills, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills, with ability to develop, assess, and synthesize information from a wide variety of sources on a wide range of issues in order to develop sound recommendations.
Ability to function independently in a complex institutional environment and manage multiple assignments, competing priorities, and rapid deadlines.
